what: Planned log PR runs on the active design or implement branch
scenario_or_breakage: In nested /design, branch_info_supplied=true means /implement's active feature branch is reused; the planned publish step commits logs, opens or reuses a PR, admin-merges it, and deletes the branch before /implement has run. In standalone /design from main, CURRENT_BRANCH can also be stale after Step 1 creates a new branch.
suggested_fix: Do not publish from CURRENT_BRANCH. Create a dedicated larch-log branch per design run from the default branch, validate the checked-out branch before push, and skip/route differently when SESSION_ENV_PATH is non-empty.

what: create-pr existing-PR fast path can admin-merge unrelated work
scenario_or_breakage: create-pr.sh returns PR_STATUS=existing for any open PR on the current branch, and the plan explicitly proceeds to gh pr merge on that PR number. A user running /design on a branch that already has an implementation PR would merge all branch contents with --admin, not just design logs.
suggested_fix: Require a dedicated log branch and reject PR_STATUS=existing unless the head branch, title, and diff are exactly the expected design-log PR; preferably avoid create-pr.sh's existing-PR path for this workflow.

what: Raw sidecar files would be committed without existing sidecar trimming
scenario_or_breakage: The plan copies all depth-1 DESIGN_TMPDIR files with only tmpdir and secret redaction, including .meta and JSON sidecars. Existing committed run-log policy strips CMD_JSON from .meta and removes top-level .result from output JSON because those fields can contain full prompts, commands, or raw model output not intended for logs.
suggested_fix: Use an explicit allowlist plus the existing larch-log sidecar trimmers, or factor stage_round_artifact-style handling into a shared helper and fail closed on trim failure.

what: The Step 5 snippet calls plugin scripts through PATH or relative cwd
scenario_or_breakage: tracking-issue-write.sh is not called with ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts, and scripts/design-log-publish.sh is relative to the operator cwd. In plugin-consumer mode this can fail with command-not-found or execute a consumer repo script with the same path.
suggested_fix: Use "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/tracking-issue-write.sh" and "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/design-log-publish.sh"; inside the new script, resolve sibling helpers from its own SCRIPT_DIR.

what: Warning paths use print inside a bash snippet
scenario_or_breakage: The planned Step 5 code block uses print for warnings. Bash 3.2 does not provide print, so the warning path can produce command not found and, depending on surrounding set -e behavior, mask the original best-effort failure.
suggested_fix: Use printf '%s\n' '...' in bash snippets, or keep Print directives outside fenced shell code.
